subject: Escalation: request for multi-year price-stability and uplift waiver
body_plain:
Message 1 - 2026-11-24 09:12 PST
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Proposal: 3-year rate lock + uplift cap option

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the time last week. As discussed, attached is a formal 3-year proposal that aims to preserve price stability for NimbleHealth while keeping us within acceptable margin ranges. Key commercial highlights: 
- Term: 36 months starting Jan 1 2027
- Price lock: current list rates locked for the first 24 months
- Uplift cap: max annual increase of 5% in years 3 (i.e., year-over-year increases capped at 5%)
- Renewal protection: automatic renewal unless either party provides 90 days notice; renewal increases capped at the uplift cap unless both parties agree otherwise

Attachments: nimble_proposal_3yr_v2.pdf, redwood_rate_table.xlsx

I want to be explicit: the uplift cap and price lock above are non-standard and will require executive signoff from our Deal Desk / Finance. I'm escalating internally today and expect to come back with a final answer within 48–72 hours.

If the above looks directionally correct, we'll prepare a redline-friendly redlined copy for your contracts team.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0189

-----
Message 2 - 2026-11-25 11:03 PST
From: Priya Sharma <priya@nimblehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@nimblehealth.com, Daniel Park <daniel.park@nimblehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Proposal: 3-year rate lock + uplift cap option

Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround; the term structure looks promising. Two asks from our procurement side before we route to legal: 
1) Can you tighten the uplift cap to 2% year-over-year for the renewal and the third year? 5% would materially exceed our budget plan.
2) Can you add a mid-term exit provision if there is a material change in billing model or a material availability breach (we'd need a 6-month cure window)?

If Redwood can accept the 2% cap and the availability carve, we can move to an expedited signature path (we have internal sponsorship from the CIO).

Thanks —
Priya
Procurement, NimbleHealth
priya@nimblehealth.com

-----
Message 3 - 2026-11-26 08:47 PST
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: NimbleHealth asks — need exec approval for 2% cap & exit clause

Rishi —

Escalating NimbleHealth. They are pushing for a 2% uplift cap (vs our proposed 5%) and a mid-term availability exit (6-month cure window). Deal highlights: 
- ARR profile: starting ~$1.8M ARR first 12 months, ramping to ~2.6M by year 3 (see redwood_rate_table.xlsx)
- Contract term: 36 months; Nimble wants deeper price certainty due to their budgeting cycle
- Customer willingness: CIO sponsorship; procurement is comfortable moving fast if we concede the two asks

Key asks for exec decision: 
A) Approve 2% uplift cap for years 2–3 and renewal OR counter with 3%?
B) Approve a limited mid-term exit tied to availability SLA breach with 6-month cure window? If yes, define guardrails (e.g., >3 outages or P0 > 12 hours in a rolling 90-day period).
C) Any other commercial conditions we should attach (e.g., minimum annual commit, onboarding fee)?

I've attached the proposal and rate table. Finance needs to confirm margin impact but this is trending toward mid-single-digit EBITDA impact over the 3-year horizon if we accept 2% and a generous exit.

Appreciate a quick read — they're ready to sign if we can move.

Best,
Vanessa

-----
Message 4 - 2026-11-27 10:15 PST
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Fwd: NimbleHealth asks — need exec approval for 2% cap & exit clause

Team —

Thanks for the context. I'm inclined to approve a concession but with controls. Recommendations: 
- Uplift cap: approve 3% annual cap (years 2–3) rather than 2%. This keeps us within forecasted margin and is a strong commercial move.
- Price lock: keep the initial 24-month firm lock as proposed.
- Exit clause: agree to a tightly scoped availability-based escape: triggers allowed only for sustained, repeatable P0 incidents (defined as >6 hours downtime impacting live inference >50% of traffic) OR three discrete P1 incidents within a 90-day rolling window. We will require a 90-day remediation window, not 6 months.
- Safeguards: require a 12-month minimum annual commitment (annual true-up invoice) and onboarding professional services fee ($45k) to offset one-time integration costs.

Marissa — pls confirm with Finance that 3% + $45k onboards keeps the EAC margin above our threshold. Markus — please sign off on the availability trigger language if acceptable, otherwise escalate to CFO.

If we get signoff, Vanessa: respond to Priya with approved concessions and request an expedited SOW + PO.

Rishi
VP, Sales

-----
Message 5 - 2026-11-29 15:40 PST
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: RE: RE: Fwd: NimbleHealth asks — need exec approval for 2% cap & exit clause

All —

Reviewed the numbers with Finance. Conditional approval provided with the following mandatory requirements: 
1) Uplift cap set to 3% per year for years 2 and 3 (no retroactive adjustments).
2) Price lock for first 24 months remains as proposed.
3) Availability escape: accept Rishi's tightened language (90-day remediation window) with precise SLA thresholds to be added to Schedule A.
4) Minimum annual commit: customer must hit at least 85% of committed spend each contract year or the uplift protection is voided for the next renewal (standard clawback).
5) Professional services fee of $45,000 to be invoiced on contract execution and non-refundable.

Once contracts confirms Schedule A language and Procurement signs PO, Finance will clear final countersignature. Please attach signed_ma_summary.pdf to the HubSpot deal record as proof of approval.

-Markus
Head of Revenue Operations (acting CFO)
markus.klein@redwood.com

-----
Message 6 - 2026-11-30 10:05 PST
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@nimblehealth.com>
Cc: contracts@nimblehealth.com, Daniel Park <daniel.park@nimblehealth.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Proposal: 3-year rate lock + uplift cap option

Priya —

Thanks for your patience. Good news: Redwood can approve a commercial package that preserves meaningful price stability while protecting our mutual interests. Final approved summary (for inclusion in the contract): 
- Term: 36 months (01/01/2027–12/31/2029)
- Price lock: current rates locked for first 24 months
- Uplift cap: 3% maximum annual increase in years 2 and 3; renewal increases capped at 3% unless mutually agreed otherwise
- Availability escape: narrowly scoped SLA-based exit with a 90-day remediation window (Schedule A will define P0/P1 thresholds; contracting to provide wording)
- Minimum annual commit: 85% of annual committed spend required to preserve uplift protection; standard clawback applies if not met
- Professional services: $45,000 invoiced at execution (non-refundable)

If Nimble accepts the framework above, we will circulate a redline-ready contract with Schedule A and the PO path for signature. 

Next steps: 
1) Priya/Contracts — confirm acceptance and share PO timeline.
2) Vanessa — I will attach signed_ma_summary.pdf to the HubSpot deal and route to legal for final Schedule A wordsmithing.

Looking forward to closing this.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

[Attachments referenced: nimble_proposal_3yr_v2.pdf (proposal), redwood_rate_table.xlsx (cost model), signed_ma_summary.pdf (internal approval stub)]
